title: marrubium peregrinum var. creticum
intro: Marrubium peregrinum var. creticum, commonly known as Cretan grey-leaved horehound, is a plant species in the mint family that is native to the island of Crete in Greece. This plant is used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of digestive issues, such as diarrhea, and respiratory problems, such as coughs and bronchitis. The therapeutic actions of Cretan grey-leaved horehound include its anti-inflammatory, antispasmodic, and expectorant properties, which may help to soothe and calm the digestive and respiratory systems. The bioactive constituents of this plant include iridoids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are believed to contribute to its medicinal properties.
